capacity.realized_capacity_note: The 3.23 req/s model capacity assumes decode batches run full (64 rows). The measured loop cannot sustain that: padded-cache rebuild cost scales with concurrency x context (and needs ~2x the KV when the padded batch is transient), so the first overloaded cell hit CUDA OOM at max_running=96 and the realized equilibrium was ~1.5-1.6 req/s. The frozen ladder is unchanged; two lower control points were added after measuring this, before any policy run completed.

cells.notes: low-load controls (0.34x and 0.17x nominal capacity, i.e. ~0.7x and ~0.34x the measured realized capacity of ~1.6 req/s). Added after measuring that realized capacity, before any policy run completed, to bracket a genuinely unloaded regime. Limited to 150 requests because low load means a long arrival span. All cells limited in request count and capped at max_running=48 (the padded-cache rebuild needs about twice the KV when the padded batch is transient; max_running=96 hit CUDA OOM at ~1.9k context). Caps are identical for every policy.

ordering_note: Cells are ordered most-informative-first. The realized capacity of this executor is well below the cost model (the padded-cache rebuild), so the frozen ladder runs from about 1x to about 4x realized capacity: at the nominal saturated point (rate-scale 0.529) the first complete run of the earlier ordering gave attainment 0.014 and TTFT p50 26 s, i.e. deep overload, while at rate-scale 0.2 the queue stays empty. The near-knee cells therefore carry the SLO comparison and the deep-overload cells act as the negative control. That single partial run (one policy, so not a cell) is kept in run-output/superseded/ for transparency and is excluded from the analysis.
